newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees more positive tone on BA/American deal.
newsitem.headline: EU sees more positive tone on BA/American deal.

text.p: European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert was optimistic on Thursday about talks on competition problems raised by the proposed alliance between British Airways BA and American Airlines.

Van Miert told reporters the "environment" for discussions was more positive now than during the initial investigation process when the British government strongly contested the EU's right to vet the deal.

The alliance with American Airlines, a unit of AMR, ran into problems at the beginning of the year when Van Miert made it known that in his view it would restrict competition between Britain and the United States.
He particularly voiced concerns about access to London Heathrow airport, Europe's main hub for transatlantic business flights.
Van Miert said the EU executive had formulated its concerns about the deal's impact on competition and that cooperation with British authorities had "further developed".
He added that the Commission's position would be presented to the EU's consultative committee on mergers, which consists of national competition officials.

"And then...it is up to the companies...to take that into account and to tell us what they are prepared to do about it," Van Miert said. "So this is now, I think, in the air." He did not give any details on the timetable.
Asked whether there was now a more positive tone from the Commission, he said: "Well, by all sides I think."

"The environment in which we now can discuss how to sort things out is indeed more positive than (in the beginning)," he said, adding: "The main point is: will the companies concerned come up with ideas, suggestions which might meet the competition concerns."

In a preliminary ruling in December, Britain's Office of Fair Trading proposed clearing the deal on condition that the two airlines gave up 168 weekly landing and take-off slots at Heathrow. But Van Miert challenged the UK with legal action if the ruling became effective.
U.S. and British approval also hinges on the successful conclusion of an open skies agreement between the two countries. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
